CSpyBat_help.stdout:
IAR C-SPY Command Line Utility V9.5.4.2231
     Copyright 2026 IAR Systems AB.

Usage: CSpyBat can be invoked in two different ways:
  1.
    Specify all options on the command line. Besides the optional named arguments,
    there are three mandatory positional command line arguments:
      <processor dll/so filename>
      <driver dll/so filename>
      <debug executable filename>
  2.
    Specify a launch configuration file together with a launch configuration name.
    Any additional named optional arguments overrides what is specified in the configuration file.
      --launch_file <launch json filename>
      --launch_config <configuration name>

Examples:
 CSpyBat <target>/bin/lib<target>proc.so <target>/bin/lib<target>sim2.so application.out --plugin=<target>/bin/lib<target>LibsupportUniversal.so <options> --backend <driver options>
 CSpyBat --launch_file launch.json --launch_config my_config <options> --backend <driver options>

Available command line options:
--application_args[=<space-separated arguments in single string>] 
                Passes command line arguments to the debugged application.
--attach_to_running_target 
                Makes the debugger attach to a running application without resetting the target system.
--code_coverage_file <code coverage file> 
                Enables the generation of code coverage information and places it in a specified file.
--cycles <cycles> 
                Specifies the maximum number of cycles to run.
--debug_file <file> 
                Specifies the executable to debug.
--device_macro <macro file> 
                Specifies a C-SPY device macro file.
--download_only Downloads a code image without starting a debug session afterwards.
-f <file>       Extends the command line with arguments given in <file>.
--flash_loader <flash file> 
                Specifies a flash loader specification XML file.
--help          Shows this help message.
--launch_config <configuration name> 
                Specifies a configuration in the launch file to use.
--launch_file <json file> 
                Specifies a launch configuration file to use. Use "-" to read the launch structure from standard input.
--leave_target_running 
                Leaves the application running on the target after the debug session is closed.
--macro <macro file> 
                Specifies a macro file to be used.
--macro_param <name=expression> 
                Assigns a value to a C-SPY __param macro parameter.
--plugin <plugin file> 
                Specifies a plugin to be used.
--print_launch_config 
                Display the launch configuration used for the session.
--rtc_enable    Enables C-RUN runtime error checking in cspybat.
--rtc_output <output file> 
                Specifies a file for the C-RUN message output.
--rtc_raw_to_txt <file> 
                Makes cspybat act as a runtime checking message filter by reading a file as input.
--rtc_rules <rtc rules file> 
                Specifies a file for the C-RUN rules to cspybat.
--silent        Omits the sign-on message.
--sockets       Makes cspybat use sockets instead of pipes.
--timeout <milliseconds> 
                Limits the maximum allowed execution time.

All parameters supplied after '--backend' are passed to the back end.
